name: Orion
description: Orion is one of the most recognizable and prominent constellations in the night sky. Located on the celestial equator, it can be seen throughout the world. Its iconic feature is 'Orion's Belt', a trio of bright stars in a straight line.
mythology: In Greek mythology, Orion was a giant hunter who declared he could kill any animal on Earth. Gaia, the goddess of Earth, sent a giant scorpion to defeat him. Both were placed in the sky on opposite sides so they never meet.

name: Ursa Major
description: Ursa Major is famous for containing the Big Dipper asterism, one of the most recognizable star patterns. The outer two stars of the Big Dipper bowl, Merak and Dubhe, serve as 'pointer stars' to locate Polaris, the North Star.
mythology: Zeus fell in love with a beautiful nymph named Callisto. Zeus's jealous wife Hera transformed Callisto into a bear. Years later, her hunter son Arcas nearly killed her, so Zeus cast both into the sky as Ursa Major and Ursa Minor.

name: Ursa Minor
description: Ursa Minor contains the Little Dipper pattern and holds vital celestial significance because the handle ends at Polaris, the North Star, which marks true north in the northern sky.
mythology: Represents Arcas, son of Callisto. Placed in the heavens alongside his mother by Zeus to protect them from danger.

name: Cassiopeia
description: Cassiopeia is easily spotted due to its distinctive 'W' or 'M' shape formed by five bright stars. It sits opposite the Big Dipper around Polaris.
mythology: Cassiopeia was a vain queen of Ethiopia who boasted she was more beautiful than the Nereids (sea nymphs). Poseidon punished her vanity by placing her upside-down in the sky for part of the year.

name: Leo
description: Leo resembles a crouching lion. Its head and chest form a backwards question mark called 'The Sickle', anchored by the brilliant blue-white star Regulus.
mythology: In Greek legend, Leo represents the Nemean Lion killed by Hercules as the first of his twelve labor trials. Its skin was impenetrable by human weapons.

name: Scorpius
description: Scorpius truly resembles its namesake, complete with claws and a hooked stinger tail dipping near the dense starfields of the Milky Way core. Its heart glows red with Antares.
mythology: Sent by Earth goddess Gaia to humble the hunter Orion. Scorpius was elevated to the stars in honor of fulfilling his duty.

name: Cygnus
description: Cygnus features the 'Northern Cross' asterism and looks like a swan flying down the Milky Way. Its tail star Deneb forms one corner of the famous Summer Triangle.
mythology: Associated with several mythological swans, including Zeus disguised as a swan to visit Leda, and Orpheus transformed into a swan upon his death.

name: Taurus
description: Taurus is a major zodiac constellation hosting two famous open star clusters: the Pleiades (Seven Sisters) and the Hyades, which form the bull's V-shaped face.
mythology: Represents the white bull Zeus transformed into to carry Europa across the sea to Crete.
